long_biography.plain_text:
Poltava's ore-processing complex became the foundation of Kostyantin Zhevago's industrial wealth. He acquired its controlling position at twenty-two, organised the business as Ferrexpo and floated the group on the London Stock Exchange in 2007. Subsequent investment added mining capacity, improved pellet quality and extended the export network, turning a regional producer into an exporter.

After serving as chief executive, Zhevago moved to non-executive board duties and left the board. Ownership remains his economic link to the company. A trust in which he is a beneficiary wholly owns Fevamotinico, a Luxembourg vehicle holding the largest voting position in Ferrexpo. This interest leaves metals and mining as the durable centre of a portfolio that historically also included banking and other industrial enterprises through the Finance & Credit group.

uncertainties: Ferrexpo and Forbes consistently use Kostyantin Zhevago, which is adopted as the preferred professional English form. The input, Interfax-Ukraine and the existing canonical profile use Kostyantyn Zhevago; that spelling remains a valid alternate transliteration and does not indicate a different person.
The Ukrainian patronymic Валентинович is rendered Valentynovych, matching the existing canonical English full-name form. Ferrexpo and Forbes omit the patronymic in professional use.

The birth-country value Ukraine conflicts with the documented Iultin, Magadan-region birthplace. Russia is proposed because Iultin was within the Russian SFSR at his birth; Ukrainian citizenship and childhood in Ukraine are separate facts.

Ferrexpo's current disclosures identify Zhevago as one of the beneficiaries of The Minco Trust, which wholly owns Fevamotinico. They do not describe him as a current Ferrexpo director or executive, and the biographies therefore characterize his present connection as beneficial ownership rather than day-to-day management.

Operator is used for the primary wealth relationship because Zhevago took control of the Poltava asset and materially ran Ferrexpo as chief executive. His present position is non-executive beneficial ownership through the trust behind the largest shareholder.

Self-made is used without a narrower starting-position subtype. Forbes explicitly identifies the fortune as self-made, but reliable evidence located in this pass does not establish whether his starting platform was materially independent or advantaged.
Historical parliamentary and other public roles were deliberately excluded from the biographies and classifications. They do not establish current ownership or operating control of Ferrexpo.
Sanctions, allegations, investigations, litigation, controversies, private-family details and vessel research were excluded from accepted claims and biographies.
